artists.biography: The Smiths were an English alternative rock band, formed in Manchester in 1982. Based on the song writing partnership of Morrissey (vocals) and Johnny Marr (guitar), the band also included Andy Rourke (bass) and Mike Joyce (drums). Critics have called them the most important alternative rock band to emerge from the British independent music scene of the 1980s. The group was signed to the independent record label Rough Trade Records, on which they released four studio albums, several compilations, and numerous non-LP singles. Although they had limited commercial success outside the UK while they were still together, and never released a single that charted higher than number 10 in their home country, The Smiths won a significant following, and remain cult and commercial favourites. The band broke up in 1987 and have turned down several offers to reunite since then.

perplexity.description:
Best...II by the Smiths is a compilation album released in 1992 by WEA after the label acquired the band’s back catalogue. It gathers fourteen tracks drawn from the group’s short but highly influential run, and it reached No. 29 on the UK albums chart while not charting in the United States.

Musically, the set presents the Smiths in their classic rock and pop mode, with jangling guitars, sharp melodic hooks, and Morrissey’s literate, melancholy lyricism. The track selection includes some of their best-known songs, such as “Heaven Knows I’m Miserable Now,” “Ask,” “Bigmouth Strikes Again,” “There Is a Light That Never Goes Out,” and “The Boy With the Thorn in His Side,” making it a concise overview of their late-period singles and album highlights.

Though it arrived after the band had split, Best...II helped keep the Smiths’ catalog visible in the early 1990s and served as a companion to the earlier Best... I collection. Its song choices underline why the Smiths remained one of the defining British guitar bands of the 1980s, balancing caustic wit, emotional unease, and memorable pop craftsmanship.
